intent: Link to one page of a paged result set, marking the page in view.
typical_uses: A page number in the row, with the current page marked by isActive

dont_use_when.situation: A navigation link outside a pagination row

instead.target: the consuming application's own link component (a plain anchor when it has none)
instead.note: This kit ships no Link component, and no kit component is a substitute for one: navigation belongs to the app's own router.

dont_use_when.situation: A link to the previous page
A link to the next page

invariants.text: PaginationLink always renders an `a` and has no `render` prop, so the application's own router link component cannot replace the element; every anchor attribute and handler, `href` and `onClick` included, is forwarded to it.

`isActive` sets `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` on the anchor, and the active paint (pagination.module.css `.link[data-active]`: the --background fill under a --primary label) selects `data-active`; without it neither attribute is rendered.

With `square` on, the link is a fixed var(--control-height-xs) square with no inline padding, and a label wider than that does not grow it; with `square` off it keeps the same height and takes inline padding of var(--space-2), growing with its label.

anti_patterns.dont: Mark more than one link as isActive
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set isActive on the one link to the page in view; only one page is current

anti_patterns.dont: Drive page changes from onClick on an href of "#" alone
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give every link its page's real href, and intercept the click when the app routes on the client, so the link stays crawlable and can be opened in a new tab

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts aria-current="page" and data-active="true" with isActive, and neither attribute without it

good.title: A page reached through the app's client-side router

bad.title: The router link passed through a render prop
bad.why: PaginationLink has no `render` prop; it always renders its own anchor. Keep the real href and intercept the click for client-side routing.
